headlines.headline: Golden State Warriors guard Will Richard sidelined with torn ligament in thumb

images.name: Steph drops 41 points as Warriors beat Magic in OT for 7th consecutive win
images.caption: Steph drops 41 points as Warriors beat Magic in OT for 7th consecutive win

headlines.story:
SAN FRANCISCO -- Second-year Golden State Warriors guard Will Richard has a torn ligament in his left thumb that will sideline him for an undetermined stretch.

The Warriors listed Richard on the injury report Sunday with a torn ulnar collateral ligament and he was out for Monday's game against New Orleans at Chase Center as the team concludes a six-game homestand. Golden State didn't have practice or media availability Sunday, so there wasn't an immediate timetable for Richard's recovery or a known treatment plan.

Richard has been providing key minutes as both a starter and a reserve as Golden State has won seven straight games since an 0-3 start. He made two starts this past week, against Phoenix and Miami.

Stephen Curry has credited the Warriors figuring out their roles to grab some momentum after dropping the first three games.

headlines.story:
The Oklahoma City Thunder and Sacramento Kings kicked off trade season Sunday, making a deal to send second-year wing Nique Clifford to the injury-ravaged Thunder for two future second-round picks. How does Clifford help replenish the Thunder's depleted depth alongside reigning MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander?

With three months to go until the Feb. 11 NBA trade deadline, expect more deals as the season goes on. I'm grading every trade and breaking down the ramifications for all teams and players involved.

To determine each grade, I'm looking at multiple factors, including the on-court impact and ages of involved players, the cost in terms of draft picks and future financial implications, and the context of the team's short- and long-term outlooks. How risky or certain is the move? And how much does it help or hurt the team's chance to win the championship this season or beyond?

headlines.headline: Clippers beat Pelicans to end 7-game losing streak

images.name: New Orleans Pelicans vs. LA Clippers: Game Highlights
images.caption: New Orleans Pelicans vs. LA Clippers: Game Highlights

headlines.story: INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- — Darius Garland had 24 points and 10 assists, Brook Lopez added 20 points and the Los Angeles Clippers ended a seven-game losing streak with a 139-123 victory over the New Orleans Pelicans on Sunday night. Gradey Dick and rookie Keaton Wagler each scored 15 points and Rui Hachimura added 14 as the Clippers won for the first time since getting past the Sacramento Kings in the season opener. The Clippers went on a 15-6 run to open the fourth quarter to take control with a 117-101 lead and finished off the victory after failing to hold on to double-digit fourth-quarter leads in their previous two games. Trey Murphy III scored 26 points, while Zion Williamson and Jeremiah Fears each added 25 as the Pelicans lost their second consecutive game following a four-game winning streak. Saddiq Bey had 13 points for New Orleans, which was playing the opener of a two-game California trip.
